question: Do larger/more selected regions and an explicit current-planner retention proxy improve selection and future-assisted planning?
decision: Fixed last checkpoint, paired seeds and recording-cluster intervals. Visual coverage and retention are diagnostics, not proof of semantic importance. No adaptive sweep if unsuccessful.
budget_definition: K output region tokens per horizon; native area K*side^2, resolution and token budget reported separately. Encoder/current context always dense.
retention_proxy: SmoothL1 XY frozen-planner readout after unselected CURRENT latent cells are replaced by current global mean, toward unmodified planner. Selector gradient only. Not causal or future-specific labels.
scope: No new data, encoder tuning, original planner tuning, navtest or held-out evaluation. Prior K4 warmup has shared historical bias; this is a continuation test, not from-scratch optimality.
success_evidence: Learned selector beats equal-budget random/planning controls on dev planning with paired evidence; visual examples use the previously fixed six recordings, never chosen by outcome. Failure is reported without another automatic tuning loop.
